title: Visual target tracking and following
description: Visual detection and multi-object tracking help a UAV preserve a selected person's identity among bystanders and recover after occlusion.
introduction: Following a person means keeping track of who they are as well as where they are. This work combines visual detection, multi-object tracking and UAV motion to maintain target identity through changing viewpoints and temporary occlusion.

problem.heading: Follow the same person through a changing scene.
paragraphs: A target can become partly hidden, disappear behind an obstacle or move close to other people. A following UAV must avoid switching to a bystander when the original target becomes visible again.
The perception system and the flight controller therefore face connected tasks: preserve identity, estimate target motion, and move the UAV so that observations remain useful.

approach.heading: Use the other targets as information.
paragraphs: YOLOv8 detections are combined with the BoT-SORT and ByteTrack multi-object trackers. Information about multiple people supports re-detection of the selected target after partial or complete occlusion.
A depth-sensing module improves distance estimation when available. A three-dimensional following controller reacts to target speed and direction while seeking to maintain line of sight.

steps.text: Track multiple people to support the selected target's re-detection.

steps.title: Follow in three dimensions
steps.text: Translate target information into UAV motion while maintaining visibility.

evidence.label: Simulation evaluation
evidence.text: The system was first tested in simulation, including target-following scenarios with occlusions and changing target motion.

evidence.label: Real-world tracking and following
evidence.text: The published work also evaluates real-world operation. The supplied field demonstration illustrates following and target re-acquisition among bystanders.
